scenes.narration: On 21 November, a spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Solar System planets); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal circle (Mercury) with a thin amber curved approach path ending in a closed elliptical orbit; small 'Illustration' label; label ORBIT ARRIVAL, 21 NOV. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: It arrived at a planet often thought of as a dead, battered rock. But is it?
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury enhanced color); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Large teal outline of Mercury with scattered hairline crater circles; amber question label DEAD? fading in. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow Ken Burns pan across craters, parallax dust

scenes.narration: The capture did not go perfectly. A software glitch put BepiColombo into safe mode, and the braking burn ended early.
scenes.visual_brief: Spacecraft approaching Mercury, thrust burn animation, then a halted burn.
scenes.schematic_brief: ESA-only subject, so draw a trajectory diagram: teal planet circle, teal approach arc, an amber segment marking the burn that stops short, label SAFE MODE and BRAKING BURN ENDED EARLY; 'Illustration' label. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: track along the trajectory, amber segment draws then stops

scenes.narration: Its science phase starts in April 2027, so every clue in this video comes from older data,
scenes.visual_brief: A timeline gap between arrival now and science start in April 2027.
scenes.schematic_brief: Horizontal timeline in grey: NOV 2026 arrival marker teal, APRIL 2027 science start marker amber, bracket between them; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: timeline line draws left to right, slow drift

scenes.narration: mostly from NASA's MESSENGER, which orbited Mercury from 2011 to 2015.
scenes.visual_brief: MESSENGER orbiting Mercury, real animation of the probe in orbit.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal planet with an elongated teal polar orbit ellipse and a small amber dot moving along it; label MESSENGER 2011-2015. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: In 2026, new studies added to a decade of hints that Mercury may not be fully dead.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (MESSENGER color mosaic); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Slowly rotating teal sphere with meridian hairlines and a tiny amber glint spot; no text beyond 2026. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: One of these clues is a set of bright streaks nobody can fully explain yet. Let's start there.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury colorful crater); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Crater outline in teal with thin amber streak lines down its slope and a question mark label UNEXPLAINED. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: In early 2026, a team at the University of Bern trained a machine learning tool on about one hundred thousand MESSENGER images.
scenes.visual_brief: Many MESSENGER image frames of Mercury surface, a mosaic of tiles.
scenes.schematic_brief: Grid of small teal frame outlines filling up, an amber scanning line sweeping across; big numeral 100,000 IMAGES; source label University of Bern. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow pan with parallax, scan line sweep
scenes.overlay_hint: evidence tracker: Bright streaks, Bern; count up 100,000

scenes.narration: It found about four hundred bright streaks. They sit on sun facing slopes of young craters,
scenes.visual_brief: Young crater with bright streaks on a sunlit slope.
scenes.schematic_brief: Cross-section line drawing of a crater: teal profile, sun arrow in grey from the left, amber streaks on the sunlit slope; numeral 400 STREAKS. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: and many begin at hollows, the shallow pits that dot Mercury's surface.
scenes.visual_brief: Hollows, bright shallow pits on a crater floor.
scenes.schematic_brief: Row of teal shallow pit outlines, amber streak starting at one of them; label HOLLOWS. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow pan right, pits drift past with parallax

scenes.narration: The proposed explanation is volatile loss. Gas, perhaps sulfur or other light elements, escaping from the rock and leaving streaks behind.
scenes.visual_brief: Gas-like glowing flows, a nebula-like colourful cutaway suggesting escaping gas.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal rock slab outline with amber dotted particles rising out of it, leaving an amber streak on the surface; labels GAS ESCAPES, STREAK; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: drift through luminous gas, slow zoom

scenes.narration: Now the caution. About ninety three percent of the streaks are in the north,
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury northern hemisphere seen from above the pole.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal circle split by grey equator; northern half filled with amber dots; big numeral 93 PERCENT NORTH. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow tilt from equator to the north pole

scenes.narration: and the team ties that to how well MESSENGER imaged each region.
scenes.visual_brief: MESSENGER coverage of Mercury, imaging resolution map.
scenes.schematic_brief: Flat map rectangle in grey with teal patches of image coverage, denser in the north; label IMAGING COVERAGE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: About ten percent are not in craters at all, so other mechanisms may be at work.
scenes.visual_brief: Wide plains of Mercury between craters, rolling cinematic flight.
scenes.schematic_brief: Pie or bar in grey with a 10 percent amber wedge labelled NOT IN CRATERS. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: An outside scientist called the link to volatiles plausible. Plausible. Not proven. And nobody has watched a streak form.
scenes.visual_brief: Calm still view of a crater with one streak, emphasising absence of observation.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two grey words PLAUSIBLE in teal and NOT PROVEN in amber, with a hairline scale between them; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Those hollows are a clue in their own right, and they are not new. MESSENGER found them back in 2011.
scenes.visual_brief: Hollows image from MESSENGER, bright blue-white pits on crater floor.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal pit outlines on a grey ground line, marker 2011 DISCOVERED in amber. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: What is newer is the question of how old they are.
scenes.visual_brief: Cosmic cutaway, star clusters in time-lapse feel suggesting age.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal ring with amber question mark and label HOW OLD?; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: NASA says there are almost no small craters inside the hollows. That means they are much younger than the ground around them.
scenes.visual_brief: Close-up of hollows floor with few craters versus cratered surroundings.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two panels: surrounding ground with many teal crater dots, hollow with almost none, amber outline around the hollow; labels MANY CRATERS and ALMOST NONE; source NASA. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow pan from cratered ground into the hollow

scenes.narration: The dating is uncertain, but NASA asks a bold question: may they still be forming?
scenes.visual_brief: Slow orbit view of Mercury hemisphere in colour, hollows implied by glimmer.
scenes.schematic_brief: Age bracket in grey with a wide amber range bar and an arrow, label UNCERTAIN; no dates. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: A 2025 study agrees. It found most hollows are in an early stage, and likely still evolving.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury hollows color); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Three-step growth strip in teal: small pit to larger pit, amber marker on the first stage; label EARLY STAGE; 2025 STUDY. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The authors say BepiColombo can look for change. Keep the hollows in mind. We will come back to them.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Orion Nebula Hubble); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: ESA-only subject: two overlapping orbit ellipses around a teal planet with an amber small hollow marker; 'Illustration'; label COME BACK TO THEM. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Now the second study. Mercury is shrinking. That part is not new.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury globe slowly contracting visual, lobate scarps cliffs on surface.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal circle with a slightly smaller dashed amber inner circle, arrows pointing in; label SHRINKING. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow zoom out as circle contracts

scenes.narration: As the planet cooled, its crust buckled into long cliffs called thrust faults. What is new is how much.
scenes.visual_brief: Long scarp cliff crossing a crater on Mercury.
scenes.schematic_brief: Cross-section: two teal crust blocks with one thrust over the other along an amber fault line; label THRUST FAULT. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: In September 2026, researchers at the German Aerospace Center argued that rough, rubble covered terrain hides many of these faults from view.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury Caloris color); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal fault line partly covered by an amber hatched rubble layer; label HIDDEN FAULTS; source German Aerospace Center. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Earlier estimates said Mercury lost up to about sixteen kilometres of width. The new study says up to twenty three.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury rotating while a measurement comparison builds.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two horizontal teal bars: UP TO 16 KM and amber longer bar UP TO 23 KM, grey axis in kilometres; bars grow in. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: That is more than two Everests, not removed, but squeezed, as the crust folded over itself.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful folding landscape, cosmic cutaway of Mercury terrain scale.
scenes.schematic_brief: Mountain silhouette stack of two grey peaks (Everests) beside a teal fold line; label MORE THAN TWO EVERESTS. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Let me be plain about who says what. The streaks hint at recent, and possibly ongoing, gas loss.
scenes.visual_brief: Calm panel recap: streaks study versus shrink study, with streaks imagery.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two-column table: STREAKS (amber, recent, possibly ongoing gas loss) and SHRINKING (teal); first column highlighted. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: This shrinking study is about the past. It tells us how much Mercury has shrunk over its whole history,
scenes.visual_brief: Slow long-timescale cutaway, Mercury formation era animation.
scenes.schematic_brief: Long grey timeline arrow, teal shaded span covering the entire length labelled WHOLE HISTORY, 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: not how fast it shrinks now. The question of today belongs to an older study.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury rotation, shifting to present-day focus.
scenes.schematic_brief: Same timeline as before with an amber marker on the far right labelled TODAY. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: camera slide toward the right edge

scenes.narration: In 2023, researchers at the Open University mapped hundreds of small trenches in the crust.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury color terrain); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Top-down grey surface with several parallel thin teal trench lines; label HUNDREDS OF SMALL TRENCHES; 2023. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: They estimated these features to be three hundred million years old or younger,
scenes.visual_brief: Age scale suggestion over Mercury terrain.
scenes.schematic_brief: Axis in millions of years: bracket from 0 to 300 million in amber, labelled 300 MILLION YEARS OR YOUNGER. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: and read them as a sign of contraction that is still going on.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Sun corona SDO); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal circle with inward amber arrows pulsing slowly, label STILL CONTRACTING?. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: But the team also said that this reading may be refuted by BepiColombo imagery.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Carina Nebula Webb); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: ESA-only: stylised craft icon in teal beside a camera cone in amber pointing at trenches; 'Illustration'; label MAY BE REFUTED. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: That is an honest scientist, leaving the door open to being wrong.
scenes.visual_brief: Wide cosmic nebula colours, reflective pause.
scenes.schematic_brief: Open door outline in teal with amber light spilling out; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The third area is volcanism. Ancient volcanism on Mercury is widely accepted. The open question is whether anything is active today.
scenes.visual_brief: Volcanic vent regions on Mercury, smooth plains and vents.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two-state diagram: ANCIENT in teal solid, TODAY? in amber dashed with question mark. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow fly toward a vent region

scenes.narration: In September 2026, conference abstracts suggested hints of buried volcanic ash, and of explosive eruptions at bright patches on the surface.
scenes.visual_brief: Bright patches around a vent on Mercury, pyroclastic deposits.
scenes.schematic_brief: Layered cross-section: teal surface, buried amber ash layer, small plume above bright patch; label BURIED ASH; source EPSC 2026 abstracts. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: They also described a tentative, very large cone of volcanic debris inside the Caloris basin.
scenes.visual_brief: Caloris basin, huge impact basin on Mercury.
scenes.schematic_brief: Big teal ring labelled CALORIS BASIN with a dashed amber cone shape inside labelled TENTATIVE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Be careful here. These deposits describe explosive volcanism in the past, not activity today, and their ages are uncertain.
scenes.visual_brief: Quiet Mercury surface, nothing erupting.
scenes.schematic_brief: Timeline with teal PAST span and a grey empty TODAY marker; amber caution bracket labelled AGES UNCERTAIN. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: These are also conference abstracts, not peer reviewed papers. Nobody has seen an eruption happening.
scenes.visual_brief: Solar corona colourful, cosmic cutaway.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two document icons: teal ABSTRACT and grey PEER REVIEWED struck with amber line. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: So where does that leave the label, dead planet? Let's be exact.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury globe against the dark, seen from distance.
scenes.schematic_brief: Teal circle with amber label DEAD PLANET? ringed by a thin line. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Landforms. Chemistry. Counts of small features. All of it is indirect.
scenes.visual_brief: Three evidence types: landforms, chemistry, counts.
scenes.schematic_brief: Three teal icons: landform, flask, dot-count, each joined by a grey line to an amber label INDIRECT. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow parallax drift, icons enter one by one

scenes.narration: Nobody has seen an eruption, a new cliff, or a new streak form.
scenes.visual_brief: Still, quiet space view of Mercury limb and horizon.
scenes.schematic_brief: Three empty dashed amber outlines labelled ERUPTION, CLIFF, STREAK. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: So the evidence does not prove Mercury is alive. What it does is put pressure on the word dead.
scenes.visual_brief: Planet with a tension, pressure feeling; slow close terrain.
scenes.schematic_brief: Grey word DEAD with teal arrows pushing in from both sides, amber thin crack. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The better word may be quiet. And quiet is not the same as finished.
scenes.visual_brief: Serene colourful cosmic vista, slow drift.
scenes.schematic_brief: Word QUIET in amber with a teal line beneath, grey NOT FINISHED. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: So how do we settle it? BepiColombo is a European and Japanese mission, and only the second ever to orbit Mercury.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Earth from space); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: ESA-only: two orbiter icons (European MPO teal, Japanese Mio amber) beside Mercury, labels EUROPEAN and JAPANESE, SECOND TO ORBIT; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: It launched in 2018, so this arrival took about eight years.
scenes.visual_brief: Long journey through inner solar system.
scenes.schematic_brief: Timeline 2018 to 2026 in grey, teal spiral path, amber end marker; label ABOUT EIGHT YEARS; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: ESA says the science phase should start in April 2027, though dates may change.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury glimpsed, calendar feel.
scenes.schematic_brief: Timeline with amber range bracket around APRIL 2027 labelled DATES MAY CHANGE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Now think about what its tools can add. The European orbiter carries a laser altimeter,
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Parker Solar Probe); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Orbiter icon in teal firing a thin amber laser line down to a teal surface profile; 'Illustration'; label LASER ALTIMETER. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: laser line sweeps along the terrain

scenes.narration: and study author Nishiyama told the Associated Press that it should confirm the shrinking.
scenes.visual_brief: Shrinking planet cutaway, contracting globe.
scenes.schematic_brief: Surface profile in teal, dashed amber previous profile slightly higher; label CONFIRM THE SHRINKING; source Associated Press. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: It also carries a high-resolution camera that can compare today's surface with MESSENGER's images.
scenes.visual_brief: MESSENGER camera images of surface, ready for comparison.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two side by side frames: MESSENGER 2011 to 2015 in teal, BEPICOLOMBO later in amber, arrow between; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow pan across, frames slide in

scenes.narration: And here is the callback. Remember the hollows, young and maybe still forming?
scenes.visual_brief: Hollows again, different crater view.
scenes.schematic_brief: Hollow outline in teal with pulsing amber edge; label YOUNG, MAYBE STILL FORMING. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: That is the kind of camera that could catch one changing.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Pillars of Creation); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: ESA-only: orbiter icon with amber camera cone aimed at a hollow on a teal planet curve; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The key comparison is MESSENGER, from 2011 to 2015, against BepiColombo, more than a decade later.
scenes.visual_brief: Split timeline between two missions.
scenes.schematic_brief: Timeline: teal span 2011 to 2015, amber later marker, bracket MORE THAN A DECADE; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: A second, sharper look. Comparing the two is how we can search for change.
scenes.visual_brief: Before-and-after surface comparison.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two overlaid crater outlines, teal older and amber newer, tiny offset; label COMPARE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow cross-fade wipe between two frames

scenes.narration: My guess is that if anything changes, it will be small and slow.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (aurora Earth ISS); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Tiny amber tick moving a very small distance on a teal line; label SMALL AND SLOW. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: A hollow edge that moved. A streak that was not there before.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury north polar color); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Hollow outline with amber dashed shift of the edge, then a new amber streak drawing in. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: But it is entirely possible we will see no change at all.
scenes.visual_brief: Still majestic cosmic cutaway, calm star field.
scenes.schematic_brief: Flat teal line with no change marker, label NO CHANGE; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: If nothing changes at the camera's resolution, that would at least put limits on how active Mercury can be.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury surface at resolution scale, then a limit.
scenes.schematic_brief: Axis of activity from low to high in grey; teal bracket ruling out the upper end with amber limit line; label LIMITS ON ACTIVITY. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Think about what it would mean if the edge of a single hollow had moved.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Mercury Rachmaninoff basin); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: One hollow outline with amber arrow marking the edge shift; label ONE EDGE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.
scenes.motion: slow push-in on a single hollow

scenes.narration: Not a theory about the past, but a change we could point to, between two sets of pictures.
scenes.visual_brief: Colourful cutaway (Hubble galaxy flythrough); real NASA/ESA imagery, never presented as another mission.
scenes.schematic_brief: Two overlapping frames, teal and amber, with an amber arrow pointing to the difference; label TWO SETS OF PICTURES. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: That one small shift would turn a clue into a measurement.
scenes.visual_brief: Mercury surface, measurement feel.
scenes.schematic_brief: Amber dot on a teal ruler line sliding a small step; label CLUE TO MEASUREMENT. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The next step is close. On 9 to 10 December, the two orbiters are due to separate.
scenes.visual_brief: Two orbiters separating near Mercury.
scenes.schematic_brief: ESA-only: two orbiter icons moving apart, teal and amber, with dates 9 TO 10 DECEMBER; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

director_notes: Bölümün görsel fikri: Mercury'ye 'ölü, yıpranmış kaya' bakışından 'sessiz ama bitmemiş' bakışına yavaş bir geçiş. Gerçek NASA/SVS görüntüleri (MESSENGER yörünge, Mercury dönüşü, topografya, Caloris, oyuklar, Güneş koronası, nebula uçuşları) tercih edilir; yaklaşık yarısından fazlası videodur. BepiColombo yalnızca ESA kaynaklı olduğu için o sahnelerde kod ile çizilmiş yörünge/ayrılma şeması kullanılır ve 'Illustration' etiketi taşır. Her sahnenin bir schematic_brief yedeği vardır: #05070C zemin, turkuaz özne, amber vurgu, gri eksenler, Inter, 36 px üstü etiketler, hafif akan toz. Delil sahnelerinde (3, 8, 16, 22, 35, 45) delil sayacı çıkar. Temkinli cümlelerde (kanıt değil, ipucu) sakin, yavaş hareket; kozmik ara planlar (nebula, korona, yıldız kümeleri) genel cümlelerde renk ve nefes verir. Aynı görsel işlem art arda tekrarlanmaz: video, fotoğraf ve çizim dönüşümlü gider.
